title: Mixed Allied Reactions to Pentagon Loyalty Questionnaire: Finland's Stubb Downplays Pressure as Former US NATO Envoy Daalder Warns of Alliance 'Obituary'
detail: Reactions to the Pentagon's leaked NATO loyalty questionnaire diverged sharply on August 17, 2026. Bloomberg reported that Finnish President Alexander Stubb, asked by reporters whether the US was pressuring allies with the document, said "I don't see it as pressure, it is the way the current US administration operates" — describing it as simply "the working method of the current U.S. administration" rather than coercion, and confirming Finland would respond to it even though Helsinki's position both converges with and diverges from Washington's. The same day, former US Ambassador to NATO Ivo Daalder published a sharply contrasting assessment in his "America Abroad" newsletter titled "This Is How NATO Dies," arguing the questionnaire — sent bilaterally to each of NATO's 31 other members rather than through alliance channels — creates a "prisoner's dilemma" that incentivizes individual capitals to cut side deals with Washington instead of maintaining collective solidarity, replacing NATO's foundational "common perception of the threat and deep commitment" with tests of personal loyalty to the sitting president. Daalder concluded: "Thirty-one separate loyalty tests isn't an alliance policy. It's an alliance's obituary, written one country at a time." The split reactions illustrate the range of allied responses to the Pentagon's six-month Europe force-posture review, from Nordic pragmatism to alarm among former transatlantic officials.
